messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: spike in 401s from prod-auth v2 starting ~10:02 UTC. Samples show unexpected `kid` values and a handful of leaked metadata snapshots uploaded to an internal S3 path: s3://redwood-internal-dumps/2026-03-17/auth-meta-xxxxx (partial). Tagging @oncall-sre and @secops-bot for triage.
oncall-sre: Ack. I'm on it — joining call in 2. Can someone paste the query that surfaced the S3 path?
anna: saw this in the auth-telemetry alert run. Query: ```SELECT headers.kid, count(*) FROM auth_logs WHERE status=401 AND service='prod-auth' GROUP BY headers.kid ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20;``` A handful of unusual `kid`s appear only after the 09:58 deploy.
bryce: rolling back the 09:58 job should be quick if needed. Also can flip `auth.v2_enabled=false` flag to kill the new validator path. That reduces exposure risk quickly.
secops-bot: Note: the stored snapshot contains service account ARNs + truncated refresh token traces (no full tokens visible in preview). Recommend immediate KMS key swap for signing key + rotate any accessible service account keys referenced.
diane: Legal: preserve all evidence. Do not delete the S3 objects or logs. We'll need chain-of-custody notes. Notify me if any customer PII is confirmed.
eng-platform: Running rollback dry-run now, will report ETA. Also preparing a small config patch to disable the new validator route. If we flip the flag, we should monitor 401 rate for 5m and be ready to rollback.
oncall-sre: Plan A: flip feature flag now, monitor. If 401s drop, follow with controlled rollback of the 09:58 deploy. Plan B: if flip fails, do immediate rollback. Can @anna and @bryce run the flip and the rollback respectively?
anna: flipping flag in 30s: `/reconfigure feature auth.v2_enabled false --env=prod --who=anna` (simulated command)
anna: :white_check_mark: flag flipped. Watching metrics.
anna: 2m in — 401 spike down ~85%. Latency steady. Good sign.
bryce: prepping rollback but standing down since flag worked. Will hold for 15m then coordinate gradual rollback if needed.
secops-bot: Begin KMS key rotation workflow for signing key id `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123:key/abc-123` — scheduled rotate + create a new key, update token-signing service to publish new `kid`. Steps posted to secure-runbook.
eng-platform: Pushing a small hotfix to ensure new tokens are issued with both old+new `kid` for a transition window to avoid churn. Deploying to canaries first.
legal-oncall: Confirming we have a legal hold on S3 path and logs. Don't purge anything until we confirm no customer PII.
oncall-sre: Good. Action summary: (1) flag flipped (anna) — immediate mitigation, (2) KMS key rotation initiated (secops), (3) hotfix to emit dual-kid tokens (eng-platform), (4) rollback on standby (bryce), (5) evidence preserved (diane/legal).
secops-bot: Quick note on keys: schedule sliding rotate, do NOT schedule deletion until we've validated token acceptance for 7 days. Use step: `aws kms create-key && aws kms create-alias` and update signing service alias atomically.
anna: Observability: adding a filter to scrub exposed snapshot object names from public logs and restricting S3 bucket to internal-only access. Also creating an alert for any object PUT to that prefix.
bryce: can we confirm customer impact? I don't see any customer token replays yet but the spike did correlate with a minor increase in auth failures for a small percentage of traffic (0.4%).
diane: Legal/Support: open a customer-impact review ticket, but don't send customer notices until we confirm tokens were not exfiltrated in full. Keep support on standby with templated message.
oncall-sre: I'll escalate to incident commander and spin up a short bridge for 20m post-mitigation to review telemetry and next steps. Please add all logs/commands to the incident ticket.
eng-platform: Canary hotfix passed; main deploy in 10m. We'll monitor metrics and rollback if anomalies.
secops-bot: Post-action: run the key lineage audit and produce a short report for the SOC. Adding tasks: rotate any service account keys referenced in the snapshot, revoke unused STS sessions.
legal-oncall: Thanks. If PII found, send immediate notice to legal. Otherwise we'll prepare internal memo and timeline for customers if required.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation in place. Severity: P2 (potential leak + auth disruption). Bridge scheduled in 18m. Owners: oncall-sre, secops, eng-platform, legal.
oncall-sre: closing loop here for now. If anything starts spiking again ping with :rotating_light:. Great work everyone — we'll reconvene on the bridge.
